chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from Muhammad ibn Suleiman, from Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! How did the waiting period of the divorced woman become three menstruations, or three months, and the waiting period of the woman whose husband died become four months and ten days?'
So he said: 'As for the waiting period of the divorced woman being three pure periods (Quroo'), it is for the clearing of the womb from the child.'

And as for the waiting period of the woman whose husband died, indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, stipulated a condition for the women and stipulated a condition against them. So He did not seize them with what He stipulated for them, nor was He unjust with what He stipulated against them.

He stipulated for them regarding the oath (of abstention from intercourse) four months, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'For those who swear to abstain from their wives, [let them have] a waiting period of four months.'
So He did not allow anyone more than four months regarding the oath, for His knowledge, Blessed and High, knows that it is the limit of the woman's patience from the man.
And as for what He stipulated against them, then He commanded her that she should observe a waiting period when her husband dies from her, for four months and ten days.
Thus, He took from her for him at his death what He took for her from him during his life at the time of his oath.
Allah, Blessed and High, says: 'They should keep themselves in waiting for four months and ten.'
And He did not mention the ten days in the waiting period except with the four months.
And He knew that the limit of the woman's patience is the four months regarding the abstention from intercourse.
So from that, He obligated it against her and for her.

key_terms.عِدَّةُ الْمُطَلَّقَةِ: Waiting period of the divorced woman

ai.seo_question: What is the wisdom behind the difference between the waiting period of a divorced woman and a widowed woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the three-month 'Iddah for divorce serves primarily for 'Istibra' (clearing the womb), whereas the extended four-month-and-ten-day period for widowhood reflects a divine balance of reciprocity. This duration is rooted in the principle that Allah limited the maximum period of an oath of abstention (Ila') to four months, thereby establishing the upper limit of a woman's patience for sexual abstinence, which He then extended by ten days for the widow's mourning period.
